new.analysis:
Week one back was clean. All three walk-run sessions ran as planned, the shin stayed quiet, and pain was 0 out of 10 on every run, so the next step can be small.

Your weekly report shows 15 minutes per session but not the length of each run segment. I have assumed last week's rounds were 2 minutes running and 1 minute walking. If they were shorter, keep Monday and Wednesday at the rounds that felt quiet and add the extra minute only on Saturday.

| Measure | Last week | Next week |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runs | 3 | 3 |
| Total running time | 45 min | 46 min |
| Longest continuous run | 2 min (assumed) | 3 min |

Total running time rises by about 2 percent, well under the roughly 10 percent limit. That is deliberate, because a shin that has had a stress reaction needs more than one clean week before the load climbs.

Every run stays easy, on flat ground with soft surfaces where possible. There are no hills, strides or speed work until four pain-free weeks in a row are done. The morning shin check matters more than how a run feels.

The stop rule still applies. If any run reaches pain above 3 out of 10, or the shin is worse the next morning, repeat this week instead of stepping up. Pain at 3 out of 10 or below that settles by the next morning allows the next small step.

Effort was 3 out of 10 across all three runs, so the pace was comfortably easy. Heart rate rose 3.6 bpm during Saturday's run, so keep it under 135 when the run segments get longer. Your nerves are normal after ten weeks off, and sleep averaged 7.5 hours, which supports the load.

Keep the calf and hip routine on the two non-run days, exactly as your physio set it. Both routine sessions were done last week, and that habit matters as the running time grows.
